Federweisser (New Wine)

Served at: St. Martin's Day (Martinstag)

Serves 4-6 (from a 1-liter bottle)Prep 5 min

Federweisser is a young, partially fermented grape must, a seasonal autumnal delight in Germany and Austria. Its cloudy appearance and effervescent, sweet-tart taste mark the transition from grape harvest to finished wine. While Martinstag (St. Martin's Day) in November is a time for goose, Federweisser is often enjoyed throughout the autumn season, including around this festive period, celebrating the bounty of the harvest.

Ingredients

  • 1 bottle (1 liter) Federweisser (white or red)

Method

  1. Federweisser is actively fermenting, so it is crucial to store the bottle upright and never seal it tightly; the cap or cork will be loose or perforated to allow gases to escape.
  2. Carefully transport the bottle, keeping it upright to prevent leaks.
  3. Chill the Federweisser in the refrigerator for at least 2-3 hours before serving; it is best enjoyed cool, but not ice-cold, to appreciate its complex flavors.
  4. Just before serving, gently invert the bottle a few times to redistribute the yeast sediment, which contributes to its cloudy appearance and flavor.
  5. Pour the Federweisser into sturdy wine glasses or tumblers, filling them about two-thirds full.
  6. Serve immediately and enjoy its effervescent, sweet, and slightly alcoholic character.

Tips

  • Due to ongoing fermentation, Federweisser continues to develop; enjoy it within a few days of purchase for optimal freshness and flavor.
  • The alcohol content increases as it ferments, ranging from around 4% to 11% ABV.
  • Traditionally, Federweisser is paired with savory dishes like Zwiebelkuchen (onion tart), Flammkuchen (Alsatian tart), or roasted chestnuts, which beautifully complement its sweetness.
